subject: asp-es
title: ASP.ES.------AF.DY.
description: Diagram in SD(SY)-22, where Braxton argues that 'the significance of a given spectacle diversion lies in its ability to progressionally re-dictate the reality dynamics of its time zone — or focus.' (C)ASP-ES (aspect essence — the focusing on one part as if it were the whole) is crossed with AF-DY (affinity dynamics): the question is what aspect-essence compression does to affinity dynamics across the culture. The graph is hub-spoke around (c)asp-es, which fans into LK-IMP (linkage implications), AF-DY (the crossing partner — itself a hub in the lower diagram), and four parallel sub-nodes through AF-DY: (R)INT (the reality of intention), MTA-IMP (meta-implications), LANG-DY (language dynamics), VT-ATT (vibrational attitude), and PROJ-DY (projectional dynamics). INFO-DE (information degrees), IST-S-ALGN (isolated systematic alignment), and MT-TFS-AT (multi-transfer shift activity) feed AF-DY from below. Structural argument: aspect-essence compression as a *conceptual* move (the (c) prefix) does not merely block affinity dynamics — it routes affinity dynamics through linkage-implications into the meta-implication / language-dynamics / vibrational-attitude / projectional-dynamics chains. The diagram exposes the structure of how spectacle-driven cultures redistribute affinity onto surface variables rather than essence ones.
